ceiling_directive: Complete the eight-branch positive-real projection analysis for the four-node fork over every full-dimensional chamber, producing either a chamberwise dense realization cover or a verified full-dimensional separator against the original five covariance equations.
improvement_directive: Classify the projected feasible union of all eight two-scalar fork systems over the full true-parameter domain and prove the resulting density or separation conclusion chamber by chamber. This would convert the current pointwise collision into an actual covariance-frontier theorem on the same graph pair.
critique: The note proves a general terminal-copy/affine characterization of corrected actual-row compatibility, an arithmetic per-candidate algorithm, and a concrete refutation of the published Theorem 3.15, but these constitute a narrow correction rather than the advertised covariance information frontier. For covariance information it proves only a finite branch reduction and a one-parameter pointwise collision; it explicitly leaves undecided whether the candidate belongs to the chamberwise generic class \(\mathsf{Cov}_2(G)\), so no generic strictness or equality frontier is delivered. The proposed square-mixing equality and the all-graph non-QE positive-real criterion from the project brief are absent, while recovery of the aligned factorization datum is treated as an input rather than established within the note. The claim that higher cumulants remove the displayed alternative is therefore conditional on access to that aligned factorization and is stronger operational language than the proved covariance-versus-input separation. The highly elaborate definitions and repeated reductions obscure the limited delivered endpoint, and the absence of a generic frontier result or practical demonstration caps the leading-journal score. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.4 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
